candidates: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:50 - Async legacy writes use the request context, so they are cancelled when the request ends.. Each goroutine builds its timeout from the request `ctx` using `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, so it also inherits that context's cancellation. The apiserver cancels the request context as soon as the handler returns, which happens right after the goroutine starts. Legacy Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection will then often fail with `context canceled`, and legacy storage quietly falls out of sync. That defeats the "write to legacy as a safe measure" goal. The same problem is at lines 108-114, 134-141 and 161-167. Fix: start from `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` and apply the timeout to that.
